summary: 2 blocking findings reviewed; both require small spec changes to define durable review stop state and child-to-wrapper provider failure signaling.

items.title: Provider and input failures have no durable stop-state path
items.rationale: The finding blocks implementation because next-action and status run after the failed review process exits. Provider/input failures do not consume reviewRetry, so maxAttempts metrics cannot reconstruct their stop reason.
items.evidence: spec.json R3/R5/R6 require recovery details in later CLI calls, while overview.data_flow does not define where provider/input stop state is persisted or cleared.

items.title: Provider failure classification lacks a child-to-wrapper contract
items.rationale: The finding blocks reliable classification because provider failures originate inside the child review command and Agent layer, while the run-review wrapper receives only subprocess status/stdout/stderr unless a structured signal is defined.
items.evidence: spec.json R1/R2/R3 require machine-processable provider/input classifications, but modules/data_flow/tasks do not specify whether src/flow/commands/review.js emits a marker for src/flow/lib/run-review.js.
